segments.textEn: I'm travelling on Monday afternoon, so I hope to collect my camera before then. Could you check whether the repair will be finished in time? I haven't received an update yet.
The technician is still testing it. I can check the repair notes now, but I cannot promise a collection time until the final test is complete.
Is the remaining test a routine check, or has it revealed another fault? I need to weigh the uncertainty before deciding whether to arrange different equipment.
It is a routine reliability check. The notes do not yet contain a final result.
If the test takes longer, is there another way to take photographs during my trip? I would rather hear the options now than assume my own camera will be ready.
We sometimes have loan cameras, although I need to check the equipment list before offering one. The list is kept at the service desk, and I can ask the supervisor about it.
Would a loan depend on the equipment being available and on the length of my trip? I can explain my requirements before you check.
Yes. Please tell me how long you would need it; availability still has to be verified.
I would need it for three days. Please check both the repair and the loan equipment. I will return after lunch to hear what you find; neither option is confirmed yet.
Certainly. I will ask the technician for the test result and check the loan list with the supervisor. We can discuss the available options when you return, without making a reservation now.
That seems sensible. An honest update will help me choose between waiting for my camera and making separate arrangements, even if the answer remains uncertain.
I understand. I will distinguish the confirmed test result from any options that are still tentative.

segments.textEn: The community centre is holding a plant-care workshop this Saturday. I have been looking for a way to keep my balcony plants healthy. Would you be interested in coming with me?
I would. My herbs keep drying out, and I would like some practical advice. Do you know what time the workshop begins?
It starts at ten in the morning and lasts ninety minutes. The organiser provides the pots, but everyone needs to bring a small plant from home. I could bring my basil.
Ten works for me. I can bring my mint plant, so we will each have something to practise with. Shall we meet outside the centre fifteen minutes before it starts?
Yes, let's meet at a quarter to ten outside the centre. Entry costs six pounds each, and the money goes towards new tools for the community garden.
Yes, a quarter to ten outside the centre works for me. I will pay at the door and bring a notebook for the advice. I'm looking forward to learning something useful together.
